marks.gloss_en: מכלל: so rinsing the whole body is fine even ab initio
דתניא: R' Meir forbids rinsing in hot and cold, R' Shimon permits, R' Yehuda forbids hot and permits cold -- only R' Shimon permits the rinsing the mishna implies
by implication: to rinse one's whole body is fine even ab initio
R' Yochanan: they taught [the prohibition] only of [inducing vomiting with] a drug
תא שמע דאמר שמואל: כולהו שקייני מדיבחא ועד עצרתא מעלו -- the healing season runs up to Atzeret, so Atzeret would close the twenty-one days
דילמא: there [drinks], the cooler the world the better; but here it is because of the heat -- the warmer the world the better
R' Yochanan: it is forbidden [on Shabbat] to stand on the floor of Deyomset

והיינו דתנן -- and this is what we learned: R' Elazar ben Arakh, away from a place of Torah, lost his learning, as R' Nehorai's dictum says (no SupportKind names והיינו דתנן; svara is the generic kind)
R' Nehorai: exile yourself to a place of Torah, and do not say that it will come after you, for your companions will establish it in your hand; and do not rely on your own understanding
R' Chelbo: the wine of Perugaita and the water of Deyomset deprived Israel of the ten tribes
R' Elazar ben Arakh happened to come there; he was drawn after them, and his learning was uprooted
מאי טעמא? משום פיקא -- the mishna's prohibition is because of the mud
what is the reason? because of the mud
והאנן תנן: אין מעצבין! -- we learned in the mishna that one may not align [an infant]
התם בחומרי שדרה, דמיחזי כבונה -- there [the mishna speaks] of the spine's vertebrae, for it looks like building (= p_okimta_chumrei_shidra, p_chumrei_shidra_kebone)
R' Yochanan: swaddling an infant on Shabbat is fine
the first tanna: one may not scrape with a scraper on Shabbat
רבי -- דתניא: Rabbi and his fellows carried oil and towel from courtyard to roof to enclosure, to the spring where they bathed
שמואל -- דאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: one dries with a towel and brings it home
רבי יוחנן -- דאמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: the halakha is, one dries with a towel and brings it home
Rabbi: when we studied Torah with R' Shimon in Tekoa, we would carry oil and a towel from courtyard to roof and from roof to enclosure, until we reached the spring in which we bathed
ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי? והאמר רבי יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה (p_halakha_kistam_mishna), ותנן: ונסתפג אפילו בעשר אלונטיות לא יביאם בידו -- an anonymous mishna forbids it
ההוא -- כבן חכינאי מתני לה: R' Yochanan teaches that clause as ben Chachinai's, so it is not an anonymous mishna for him (= p_ry_kben_chachinai)
R' Yochanan: the halakha follows an anonymous mishna
the first tanna: one dries himself with a towel and leaves it in the window
R' Yochanan: bath attendants may bring women's bathing garments to the bathhouse, provided they cover their heads and most of [their bodies] with them
the first clause teaches a novelty: even these [ten towels], which have not much water in them -- since he is one, he will come to wringing
the baraita: one may smear [oil] and rub the abdomen on Shabbat
